title: Salt Bread (Shio Pan)
summary: Japanese-style salted butter rolls with a crisp buttery bottom, a soft interior, and a sprinkle of coarse salt.

steps.description: Mix 300 g bread flour, 18 g sugar, 5 g salt, and 4 g instant yeast in a large bowl. Pour in 180 ml lukewarm milk and mix into a dough. Knead for about 5 minutes, then incorporate 20 g softened unsalted butter and knead for another 5–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Shape the dough into a ball, place in a bowl, and cover. Let rise in a warm place (around 26–28°C / 79–82°F) for 60–90 minutes until roughly doubled in volume.

Gently press the dough to release excess gas and divide into 8 equal pieces. Shape each into a ball, cover, and rest for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, cut 64 g chilled unsalted butter into eight long 8 g pieces.

Roll each dough piece into a long, narrow triangle about 25 cm (10 inches) long. Place an 8 g piece of cold butter at the wide end, enclose the butter, and roll toward the tip snugly. Position the tip underneath each roll. Repeat with the remaining dough.

Space the 8 rolls on a parchment-lined baking sheet and cover. Let rise in a warm spot for 35–50 minutes until about 1.5 times their size. Toward the end, thoroughly preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F). Lightly brush the tops with about 1 tsp water and distribute about 2 g coarse salt over the rolls.

Bake on the middle rack at 210°C (410°F) for 15–18 minutes, until deeply golden on top and underneath. Transfer to a wire rack and cool for about 5 minutes to keep the bottoms crisp. Some butter leaking during baking is normal.
